verdict.summary: Intel’s Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 25% to $16.1B and non-GAAP EPS reached $0.42, but GAAP EPS remained a $2.16 loss and trailing net margin is deeply negative. The investment case combines a recovering product roadmap with foundry optionality, while the actual economics are dominated by fabrication underutilization, capital intensity and external-customer execution. August financing materially reset the denominator: Intel completed 242,105,262 common shares at $95 for $23B gross proceeds. That was a primary common offering, not an ATM; the S-3ASR was registration capacity and the April 424B5 filings were straight debt. The 58/100 score appropriately remains capped by losses, leverage and dilution even though liquidity improved. Q3 guidance of $15.8B-$16.8B revenue, 41% GAAP gross margin and $0.31 GAAP EPS offers a measurable recovery test. The setup remains watch-only at the preserved $92.68 activation. New capital buys execution time, but it does not prove foundry utilization, process yields or sustainable free cash flow.

business.overview:
Intel sells client and data-center processors, networking and edge products while building a contract foundry business around its manufacturing process and packaging assets. Revenue depends on PC and server unit demand, product mix, competitive performance, wafer utilization and external foundry customers. Fabrication fixed costs make yields and utilization decisive for GAAP margins.

The AI transmission channel is mixed. Xeon processors, accelerators, networking and advanced packaging participate in AI servers, while Intel Foundry seeks external wafer and packaging volume from chip designers. Unlike a merchant accelerator leader, Intel must fund leading-edge process nodes before customer ramps are certain, so AI capex can initially increase losses rather than earnings.

What breaks is roadmap or utilization execution. Delayed nodes, weak yields, customer concentration, export controls or share loss to AMD and Arm can leave expensive fabs underloaded. The $23B common offering extends runway but dilutes existing holders by 242.1M shares and does not establish demand. Straight debt and government-linked funding add contractual or strategic constraints, while sustainable value requires foundry losses to narrow and product gross margin to recover.
business.moat: Intel’s moat is its x86 ecosystem, installed enterprise base, packaging capability and ownership of scarce leading-edge fabrication assets. The moat is impaired when process execution lags; fabs become fixed-cost liabilities unless internal and external wafer volume reaches adequate utilization.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Intel reported 5.043B common shares issued and outstanding at June 27. The completed August offering added 242,105,262 shares, implying about 5.285B post-offering basic shares, consistent with the 5.29B snapshot. Q2 diluted weighted-average shares were 5.104B because of the loss; 70M antidilutive awards, 71M contingent escrow shares and 241M unexercisable government warrants were excluded. The January 23 S-3ASR, accession 0000050863-26-000023, registered broad capacity but sold no securities by itself and is not included in the post-offering share arithmetic.

filings.finding: The Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q supports $16.1B revenue, the GAAP loss, liquidity, debt and foundry cost disclosures; it shows that product recovery has not yet produced durable consolidated GAAP profitability.
The August 12 Form 8-K confirms completion of 210,526,315 primary common shares plus the fully exercised 31,578,947-share option at $95, totaling 242,105,262 shares and $23B gross proceeds.

This final Form 424B5 covers Intel’s primary common-stock offering and underwriter option; it documents completed equity dilution and must not be classified as an ATM, secondary-only resale or straight debt.
This preliminary Form 424B5 describes the August primary common-stock offering later completed at $95 per share; it is transaction evidence, not merely undrawn shelf capacity and not debt.
The August 10 S-3ASR creates automatic registration capacity. By itself it is not an issuance, ATM program, primary or secondary sale, debt draw, warrant exercise or proof of proceeds.

The April 29 final Form 424B5 prices $6.5B of straight debt: $1.0B 4.650% notes due 2031, $1.0B 5.000% due 2033, $2.25B 5.300% due 2036, $1.75B 6.125% due 2056 and $0.5B 6.200% due 2066. It creates no common dilution or ATM.
The April 27 Form 424B5 is the related straight-debt prospectus rather than equity financing; it affects leverage and interest obligations, not the outstanding common-share denominator.

The FY2025 Form 10-K supplies Intel’s audited Products, Foundry and All Other reporting baseline, fabrication commitments, government incentives, debt and loss exposures; it predates and therefore does not include the August 2026 common offering.
